test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A water tank can be filled in 40 minutes by using 43 pipes of the same capacity. In how many minutes (rounded off to two decimal places) will the water tank be filled if we use 9 pipes of the same capacity as above?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the inverse proportionality rule: **M₁ × T₁ = M₂ × T₂**

Substitute values: 43 pipes × 40 minutes = 9 pipes × T₂

T₂ = 1720 ÷ 9

T₂ = 191.11 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 191.11 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of pipes (n₁) = 43

Initial time taken (t₁) = 40 minutes

New number of pipes (n₂) = 9

**Formula Used:**

Work = Number of pipes × Time taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of tank = 43 × 40 units

⇒ Total capacity = 1720 units

⇒ Time required by 9 pipes = Total capacity ÷ 9

⇒ Time = 1720 ÷ 9

⇒ Time = 191.1111... minutes

⇒ Time ≈ 191.11 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 191.11 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion in Pipes

When the capacity of each pipe is constant, the **number of pipes** is inversely proportional to the **time taken** to fill the tank (n ∝ 1/t).

Work and Efficiency

Total work is constant in such problems, following the chain rule: **M₁D₁H₁ = M₂D₂H₂**, where M represents the number of workers/pipes.

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

If one pipe fills a tank in 'x' minutes, then its 1-minute work is 1/x of the total tank capacity.</p
